back: n = c ÷ v: the speed of light in a vacuum divided by its speed in the material. Always greater than 1.
n₁ sin i = n₂ sin r. Light entering a higher-index medium bends toward the normal; leaving it, light bends away from the normal.
The angle of incidence (in the denser medium) beyond which light is totally internally reflected. sin c = n₂ ÷ n₁; about 41.8° for n = 1.50.
Approximately 380–760 nm (violet to red). Shorter wavelengths are refracted more than longer ones.
Unit of lens power: the reciprocal of the focal length in meters. F = 1 ÷ f.

front: Focal length of a +4.00 D lens

back: The curvature of a wavefront, in diopters = 1 ÷ distance (m). Diverging light is minus, converging light is plus, parallel light is zero.
V = U + F: image vergence = object vergence + lens power.
6 m (20 ft) or more; light from that distance is treated as parallel (vergence ≈ 0).
F = (n′ − n) ÷ r, with r in meters. For a lens surface in air: F = (n − 1) ÷ r.
F₁ + F₂: front surface power plus back surface power. Ignores thickness.
Convex front and concave back. The standard form for modern spectacle lenses.
During hand neutralization, a minus lens gives 'with' motion and a plus lens gives 'against' motion.
Rotating a lens makes cross-target lines tilt toward and away from each other. Indicates cylinder.
The meridian with no cylinder power. Maximum cylinder power is 90° away. Axes are written 1–180.
1) New sphere = sphere + cylinder (algebraically). 2) Change the cylinder sign. 3) Change the axis by 90°.
SE = sphere + (cylinder ÷ 2). Example: −3.25 −1.50 × 180 → −4.00 D.
Diagram showing the power in each principal meridian. The sphere is in the axis meridian; sphere + cylinder is 90° away.
F_θ = S + C sin²θ, where θ is the angle between that meridian and the cylinder axis.
One principal meridian is myopic and the other hyperopic, e.g., +1.00 −2.00 × 090.
One meridian is emmetropic and the other myopic, e.g., plano −1.50 × 180.
Both meridians are hyperopic but unequal, e.g., +3.00 −1.00 × 180 (+3.00 and +2.00).
The vertical meridian is steepest. Corrected by minus cylinder at an axis near 180 (plus cylinder near 090).
Displaces an image 1 cm at a distance of 1 m.
Light bends toward the base; the image appears displaced toward the apex.
Δ = c × F, where c is decentration in centimeters and F is the power in diopters in that meridian.

front: Base direction in a plus lens
back: Base points toward the optical center (plus = two prisms base to base).

front: Base direction in a minus lens
back: Base points away from the optical center (minus = two prisms apex to apex).
c = Δ ÷ F (cm). Plus lens: move the OC in the direction of the desired base. Minus lens: move the OC opposite the desired base.

front: OCs too wide in plus lenses
back: Base-out prism. (Plus OCs too narrow → base in.)

front: OCs too narrow in minus lenses
back: Base-out prism. (Minus OCs too wide → base in.)
Resultant = √(V² + H²); angle from horizontal = tan⁻¹(V ÷ H).
Vertical = P × sin θ; horizontal = P × cos θ.

front: 360° base notation (TABO, viewed facing the patient)
back: 90° = base up, 270° = base down. OD: 0° = base in, 180° = base out. OS: 0° = base out, 180° = base in.
Divide equally with the same base direction: 4Δ BO = 2Δ BO OD + 2Δ BO OS.
Divide with opposite bases: 2Δ BU OD = 1Δ BU OD + 1Δ BD OS.
Find the prism in each eye with Prentice's rule using the 90° meridian power at the reading depth (often 10 mm). Same base direction → subtract; opposite → add.

front: Why vertical prism is poorly tolerated
back: Vertical fusional reserves are only about 1–2Δ, much smaller than horizontal reserves.
Distance from the back surface of the lens to the front of the cornea. Typically 10–15 mm.
Becomes significant above about ±4.00 D.
Fc = F ÷ (1 − dF); d in meters, positive when the lens moves toward the eye.

front: Moving a lens closer to the eye
back: Plus lens needs more plus; minus lens needs less minus. Example: −8.00 at 13 mm → −7.25 D at the cornea.
Moving any lens away from the eye shifts its effect in the plus direction (plus stronger, minus weaker).
Power measured from the back surface; what a lensometer reads and what the Rx specifies.
Fv = F₁ ÷ (1 − (t/n)F₁) + F₂.
Used to measure the add of front-surface multifocals: place the front surface against the lens stop.
Focus the most plus lines first (sphere), then the second lines; the difference is the minus cylinder, and the axis wheel gives the axis.
s = r − √(r² − y²), where y is the semi-diameter (half the lens diameter).
s ≈ y²F ÷ 2000(n − 1), with y in mm and F in diopters; gives s in mm.
Edge = center thickness + sag.
Center = edge thickness + sag.
Sag ∝ y², so doubling lens diameter roughly quadruples the sag.
Base curve = SE + 6.00 D.
Base curve = (SE ÷ 2) + 6.00 D.

front: Base curve of a minus-cylinder lens
back: The front spherical surface. On a toric surface, the base curve is the flattest curve.
Plots base curves that eliminate oblique astigmatism. Ostwalt (flatter) branch is used in practice; Wollaston is steeper.
Measures surface sagitta with three pins; calibrated for n = 1.53.
True power = reading × (n − 1) ÷ 0.53. Example: +6.00 on polycarbonate → +6.63 D.
SM = power factor × shape factor. Power factor = 1 ÷ (1 − hF); shape factor = 1 ÷ (1 − (t/n)F₁).
Steeper front curve, greater center thickness, or larger distance from the eye.
V = (n_d − 1) ÷ (n_F − n_C). Higher V = less dispersion and less chromatic aberration.
TCA = prism ÷ Abbe value = cF ÷ V. Grows away from the optical center.
Plus lenses → pincushion distortion. Minus lenses → barrel distortion.
Unwanted cylinder when looking obliquely through the lens periphery. Controlled by base curve selection.
Light focuses in front of the retina. Corrected with minus lenses. Far point = 1 ÷ error, in front of the eye.
Light focuses behind the retina. Corrected with plus lenses.

front: Far point of a −2.50 D myope
back: 1 ÷ 2.50 = 40 cm in front of the eye.
Age-related loss of accommodation; corrected with a plus add for near.
Add = (1 ÷ working distance in m) − (amplitude ÷ 2). Example: 40 cm, 2.00 D amplitude → 2.50 − 1.00 = +1.50.
Add the add to the distance sphere only; cylinder and axis do not change.
Approximately 3–4 mm less than the distance PD for a 40 cm reading distance.
Prism at the seg top = add × distance (cm) from seg top to seg OC. Round 22 seg with +2.00 add → 1.1 × 2 = 2.2Δ.
Executive: none (OC on line). Flat-top: minimal (OC near the line). Round: greatest (OC at seg center).
